note: THE DOCUMENT REGISTRY. Greg, S112: 'we need to put the list of our working docs in the store or a section of the sop so one doesn't get forgotten about.' Same disease as A-17 one level up - a document that is on no list goes stale silently, and nothing can report it. MEASURED THE DAY THIS WAS BUILT: 55 of 151 tracked research/kalshi/*.py files were absent from KALSHI_TRADING.md, the index whose stated job is 'every Kalshi file, what it does, current vs old'; and PLANT_MAP.md had been EDITED THAT SAME SESSION while naming none of the four plant components built in it. So mtime is not staleness - CONTENT is, and only a content gate catches this. S119: the registry was 44 entries against 236 tracked documents, so 192 carried NO class and no gate could reach them - the andon had been red for several sessions. Closed here. The 158 with a session or date suffix in the filename were classified RECORD BY RULE (the class is literally 'dated and finished'); the remaining 34 were classified by hand, and the load-bearing ones are named: the mission and the calculation contract are VAULT because they are HASH-BOUND into every run identity - S119 changed the mission and locked the spawn emitter out of two prior runs by doing so - and the five mbo_specialist files are LIVE because blind and refine read them byte-identical.

classes.LIVE: must be kept current. A gate exists where the content can be computed; otherwise the trigger is stated and the andon can only remind.
classes.RENDER: GENERATED from a store. Never hand-edit - edit the store and re-render. Gated byte-identical by store.py check.
classes.VAULT: frozen, sha256-manifested. A change is a versioned vault event on Greg's go, never an edit. Gated by verify_gold.py.
classes.RECORD: dated and finished. NEVER updated - a handoff, kickoff, drop-in, ledger or findings memo describes the session that wrote it. Editing one is falsifying the record.
classes.ARCHIVE: moved out of the live surface deliberately. Consulted, not maintained.
classes.EXTERNAL: a DELIVERED HAND-OFF from outside the session - a ChatGPT brief, a research vendor deliverable, a task packet we sent out and got back. It is a RECORD (dated, never edited) that additionally carries RECOMMENDATIONS, so D36 binds: every numbered recommendation gets a registry id in the session the document lands, INCLUDING the ones we decide against. Audited via store/briefing_audits.json; station0/briefings reports it.

close_out_trio.note: Greg, S112: 'update all of our docs other than the 3 ending ones.' These three are written LAST, at close-out, because they summarise everything else. They are excluded from mid-session doc sweeps by design. S112 addition (Greg: 'include a doc that i can download and send to chat along with the drop ins when you're printing'): the ChatGPT hand-off ships WITH the drop-in and is GENERATED from the registry by chatgpt_handoff.py, so a finished item cannot appear in it as a live request - A-9's rule, one document over.
ships_with: DATA_POINTS.md (the master data list, needed by the triage task)

documents.role: the master pointer - one-line state, the read-first order, standing rules. Deliberately lean: it points at detail, it does not hold it.
documents.update_when: close-out only (member of the close-out trio), plus any STANDING rule change (D34 landed here mid-session because it is standing)

documents.role: THE FILE INDEX - every Kalshi file, what it does, current vs superseded. Curated prose per session, plus a GENERATED completeness appendix.

documents.role: THE SPEC BOOK, binding. Every station of the group cycle with verbatim spawn templates. Its appendix is a RENDER; the body is change-controlled prose.

documents.gate_note: the appendix is gated byte-identical against store/sop_templates.json; the prose body is change-controlled, not generated
